beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Most people think of Claude as a direct relationship: user asks, Claude answers. There is actually a layer above the conversation that most users never see. The system prompt is real. It is set before you type anything. It can restrict topics, require a persona, limit Claude to specific tasks. All of this is contractually authorized.

Three tiers. Anthropic's training-time rules are hardcoded — not even operators can override them. The operator's system prompt sits below that, setting the deployment context. The user's conversation is at the bottom. Each tier can restrict what tiers below it can do. No tier can grant permissions the tier above it did not authorize.

Operators can restrict Claude's scope. They can tell Claude to only discuss their product. They can require a persona. They can prohibit certain topics. What they cannot do: use Claude as a weapon against users — extract data from users, deceive users in ways that harm them, deny users emergency safety information. The accountability line is: operators control Claude's behavior, not Claude's loyalty.

The user floor is unconditional. Even when Claude cannot help with something because of operator restrictions, it will tell the user it cannot help here and can seek help elsewhere. It will not pretend the restriction does not exist. It will not deceive users about what it is. It will not withhold emergency safety information. This floor does not need operator permission. It is Anthropic's guarantee directly to every user.
